proved_step: LEMMA (point-count bound for non-adaptive evaluation PIT). Let p be prime, 1 <= d < p, t >= 1, N = C(t+d, d), q = p^k, and S a finite subset of GF(q)^t. Call S a hitting set for degree d if every nonzero g in GF(p)[x_1..x_t] of total degree <= d has g(s) != 0 for some s in S. Then |S| >= N/k. PROOF: the map phi: g -> (g(s))_{s in S} from V = {g: deg g <= d} to GF(q)^S is GF(p)-linear. Its kernel is zero by the hitting property. V has GF(p)-dimension N (the monomials of total degree <= d form a basis). GF(q)^S has GF(p)-dimension k|S|. So N <= k|S|. QED. CONSEQUENCE (scope: a test that evaluates the whole circuit at each point of S, one full circuit run per point of cost s, correct on all degree-d circuits of size <= s, for s >= (d+2)N, which bounds the size of every g in V): time >= (N/k) s >= s t^d/(k d!) (1+o(1)). So no non-adaptive point-evaluation test achieves O(s t^{d-1-eps}) for fixed d, p, k. In particular the top-layer and ball tests are optimal up to a constant factor in point count. This does NOT close O-E: it is a limit on one procedure class. Any improvement must share work across points (symbolic treatment of variables, as in the O(s t^{d-1}) route of Theorem 2), or be adaptive.
